findings.title: Incident opens before failure_issue_threshold consecutive failures
findings.body: In try_incident_threshold, when failure_issue_threshold is greater than 1, the code loads at most that many recent check-ins (ordered by date_added, then reversed) and returns early only if one of them is CheckInStatus.OK. It never requires the window to contain failure_issue_threshold rows. A shorter history has no OK row, so execution still sets MonitorEnvironment.status to ERROR, get_or_creates a MonitorIncident, emits issue occurrences, and sends monitor_environment_failed. A new or ACTIVE monitor with failure_issue_threshold of 3 therefore opens an incident on its first failed check-in, and stays in ERROR so later failures keep attaching occurrences, until a success resolves it. The configured consecutive-failure tolerance is ignored whenever fewer than N check-ins exist. An empty slice also falls through this check and then raises IndexError on previous_checkins[0], aborting failure processing instead of returning False. Require len(previous_checkins) >= failure_issue_threshold before transitioning.

findings.title: Non-failure check-ins count toward the failure threshold
findings.body: The threshold gate only tests whether any row equals CheckInStatus.OK. Every other status, including in-progress check-ins that are stored as MonitorCheckIn rows, is treated as part of the failure streak and also occupies a slot in the limited window. With failure_issue_threshold 2, a recent window of one in-progress check-in plus one error contains no OK row, so the environment is marked ERROR and an incident is opened after a single real failure. An in-progress row can also push an older OK check-in out of the N-row window so that success is ignored. Only error, missed, and timeout rows should count toward the consecutive-failure threshold.

findings.title: Occurrence context drops the adjusted schedule_type
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with monitor.get_schedule_type_display() so the issue event can show a human-readable schedule type. The returned dict ignores that copy and sends monitor_environment.monitor.config instead. The display conversion never reaches Kafka, so contexts.monitor.config.schedule_type stays the raw stored value (typically an integer) on every monitor incident occurrence. The payload also aliases the live config dict, so any later in-place mutation of the event context mutates the in-memory monitor. Return the adjusted copy.

findings.title: Mixed failure-reason text does not match the documented message
findings.body: get_failure_reason is shown as the Failure reason evidence on monitor issues. Its docstring specifies strings such as "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected". For more than one failure it formats each status as "%(count)d %(status)s" using the bare words missed/timeout/error, joins them, and appends a single "check-ins detected". Mixed failures therefore render as "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected" (no per-status "check-in(s)", and a plural noun for the whole list). The singular path returns "An error check-in was detected" (or missed/timeout), not the documented sentence. The docstring also misspells the summary as "humam readible". The evidence copy users see for multi-status incidents is wrong relative to the function's own contract.
